messages:
alice.m: heads up — p99 latency jumped ~120ms on prod after last night's continuous-batcher policy change. QPS looks steady, errors are flat. Observed on dedicated-1 cluster and hosted-prod.
brian.k: which policy tweak specifically? the one that adds the tentative-accept handshake to batch formation?
alice.m: yeah — rollout note said 'handshake to avoid split batches' and canary looked fine. spike started ~00:02 UTC.
sofia.r: I pulled the batch histograms. there's a fatter tail for batches of size 3-6 tokens during the interval. looks like more wait time before finalizing batches.
mateo.l: can you paste an example trace/log? I've seen weird stall patterns when handshake latency accumulates.
alice.m: trace trace-0a3c:
```
[2026-03-17T23:02:14Z] batcher: tentative_accept wait=18ms; final_accept wait=105ms; kernel_dispatch=2ms
[2026-03-17T23:02:14Z] scheduler: queue-handshake backpressure=1.2x; token_budget_alloc=low
```
brian.k: final_accept=105ms is big. kernel_dispatch is fine. Any change in KV cache behavior?
sofia.r: KV miss rate for the model jumped from ~2% to ~9% coincident with the spike window. Misses cause extra prefill which can extend handshake time.
mateo.l: so this is likely interaction: tentative-accept is waiting for KV priming + small-prefetch, causing queues to hold and handshake to amplify tail.
brian.k: can we reproduce with a load test that ramps many short-token requests?
sofia.r: yes — I'll run a synthetic with 30k reqs/s of 4-token prompts to stress that path. adding metrics: `batch.tentative_accept_ms`, `batch.final_accept_ms`, `kv.prefill_ms`, `queue.handshake_wait_ms`.
alice.m: attempted a quick canary: disabled tentative-accept on dedicated-1 (3 hosts) to see immediate impact.
deploy-bot: rollout started: disable-tentative-accept rev=rev-1987 scope=dedicated-1 (3 hosts)
alice.m: after canary p99 dropped ~90ms within 30s and stayed lower during the observation window :thumbsup:
brian.k: good sign. kernel selection didn't flip to a slower kernel during that time?
alice.m: no, kernel choices unchanged. this looks queuing/kv related.
sofia.r: next steps: lower handshake timeout, add conservative short-circuit when kv miss > 5% to avoid long tentative waits, and publish telemetry to console for this metric set.
mateo.l: I'll draft a PR to make the handshake opt-in per-model and add a revert flag. also include the playbook steps if we see this again.
alice.m: filed ISSUE-4421 with notes and links: https://rwi/co/ISSUE-4421
brian.k: assigning follow-up to eng-runtime for triage + rollout plan.
sofia.r: I also pushed a small playback script to ops repo to reproduce the pattern quickly.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: disable-tentative-accept rev=rev-1987 on dedicated-1 (3 hosts) succeeded
alice.m: thanks everyone. I'll monitor tonight and post any regressions.
